safe_temperature.temperature: 145°F (62.8°C) with a 3-minute rest time for whole beef roasts; 160°F (71.1°C) for ground beef (patties, meatloaf, meatballs)

source.name: SAFE MINIMUM INTERNAL TEMPERATURES - FDA & Beef Cookery - NDBeef
source.location: FDA Guidelines & NDBeef Food Thermometer Standards, p. 1

safe_temperature.disagreements: The FDA and USDA mandate an internal temperature of 160°F for ground beef (patties, meatloaf, meatballs) because bacteria on exterior surfaces can be distributed throughout during grinding; color is not an indicator of doneness. For tender whole-muscle roasts (rib roast, tenderloin roast, strip roast), the minimum safe temperature is 145°F with a 3-minute rest, though culinary sources pull at 135°F for medium-rare finish. In contrast, for tough, collagen-rich cuts (chuck roast, brisket, stew meat), notebook sources deliberately cook meat far past 145°F to internal temperatures of 195°F–205°F to melt collagen into gelatin and produce fork-tender, shreddable meat.

methods.cut: beef chuck roast, shoulder roast, or rump roast (3 to 4 lbs)
methods.heat: Medium-high heat skillet sear, then 325°F (163°C) covered oven or low-heat slow cooker (approx. 200°F)
methods.time: 3 to 4 hours in 325°F oven (or 6 to 8 hours on low in slow cooker)
methods.doneness: Fork-tender (internal temperature 195°F–205°F); meat separates easily when pressed with a fork
methods.rest: 10 to 15 minutes resting in braising liquid before slicing or shredding
methods.tips: Sear roast on all sides in a hot Dutch oven until a deep brown crust develops before adding liquid; place on a bed of onions and carrots; add braising liquid (beef broth, wine, or canned tomatoes) only halfway up the meat—do not submerge; braise tightly covered to trap steam.

source.name: Heart Healthy Recipe Guide - HFSA & Clover Meadows Beef
source.location: Classic Slow-Cooker Beef Pot Roast, p. 30 & Beef Braising Guide

methods.cut: beef stew meat (1-inch chuck or round cubes)
methods.heat: Medium-high heat sear, then low stovetop heat gentle simmer (185°F–200°F)
methods.doneness: Cubes are fork-tender and succulent; rich broth thickened by rendered collagen and starch
methods.rest: 5 to 10 minutes off heat before serving
methods.tips: Lightly dredge beef cubes in seasoned flour and brown in uncrowded batches; deglaze pot with broth or red wine to dissolve fond; simmer gently with root vegetables (carrots, potatoes, celery) and aromatics (thyme, bay leaf).

source.name: How to Cook Beef: Best Cooking Method for Every Cut - Clover Meadows Beef & HFSA
source.location: Stew Meat & Braising Section & Slow-Cooker Beef Stew, p. 34

methods.cut: ground beef patties (80/20 or 85/15 lean ratio, 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick)
methods.heat: Medium to medium-high heat in heavy skillet
methods.time: 3 to 4 minutes per side (approx. 8 to 10 minutes total)
methods.doneness: 160°F internal temperature measured horizontally from the side into center of patty; no pink remains and juices run clear
methods.tips: Do not press down on patties with a spatula while cooking, which squeezes out flavorful juices and creates dry burgers; flip only once after a caramelized crust forms; season exterior generously right before cooking.

source.name: Ultimate Guide to Beef | Burgers' Smokehouse & NDBeef
source.location: How to Cook Hamburgers & Ground Beef Cooking Times

methods.cut: beef rib roast / prime rib, strip roast, or eye of round (3 to 5 lbs)
methods.heat: Initial blast at 450°F (232°C) for 15 minutes, then reduced to 325°F (163°C)
methods.time: 1.25 to 1.75 hours (approx. 15 to 20 minutes per pound for medium-rare)
methods.doneness: 135°F for medium-rare (rising to 145°F during rest) or 145°F for medium
methods.rest: 15 to 20 minutes tented loosely with foil before carving
methods.tips: Place roast fat-side up on a rack in an open shallow roasting pan; insert meat thermometer into thickest part not touching bone; resting allows juices to redistribute so meat carves without pooling juice.

source.name: Ultimate Guide to Beef | Burgers' Smokehouse & NDBeef

methods.doneness: Cooked through, no pink remaining, reaches 160°F internal
methods.rest: None; drain excess rendered grease if desired
methods.tips: Let meat sear undisturbed for the first 2 minutes to develop browning fond before breaking into crumbles with a wooden spoon.

avoid.warning: Serving ground beef undercooked or rare: ground beef must reach an internal temperature of 160°F to destroy potential pathogens distributed during grinding; pink color is not an indicator of safety.
Violent, aggressive boiling of pot roasts or stews: rapid boiling causes meat muscle fibers to seize, tighten, and dry out before collagen melts into gelatin; maintain a gentle low simmer.
avoid.source: HFSA Pot Roast & Clover Meadows Beef

avoid.warning: Pressing burger patties with a spatula while searing: compresses the meat and forces out savory natural juices, resulting in dry, dense patties.
Thawing frozen beef on the kitchen counter at room temperature: bacteria multiply rapidly in the danger zone; defrost in the refrigerator or microwave immediately before cooking.
